responses.response: Use the repo’s deployment style: short environment name at the parent level, then simple child ids. A consistent set would be: Environment: `Prod` (display name `Production`). Zones: `Dmz`, `AppTier`, `ProcTier`, `DataTier`, `OpsTier`. VMs: `apiGatewayVm`, `uploadVm`, `workerVm`, `mongoVm`, `monitoringVm`. Fixes: `ProdApiVM` -> `apiGatewayVm` (or `ProdApiGatewayVm` only if you need a flat global id), `prod_upload_vm` -> `uploadVm`, `AppServers` -> `AppTier`, `MonitoringTier` -> `OpsTier` (or `Monitoring` if you want a service-specific zone name instead of a tier name). The cleanup rules are: no underscores, use `Vm` not `VM`, avoid plurals for a single zone, and do not repeat `Prod` in every child name when the parent environment is already `Prod`.

No. It is the right skill only for the naming slice of the problem. This repo supports the hierarchy `Node_Environment -> Zone -> Node_Vm -> Node_App`, and `instanceOf` belongs on `Node_App`, but asking for the full hierarchy, Markdown descriptions with IP/CPU/RAM, and links to containers is a broader deployment-modeling task. So `name-deployment-nodes` can help normalize ids such as `Prod`, `Dmz`, `apiGatewayVm`, and `apiGatewayApp`, but it is not sufficient as the main skill for the whole request.

Between the two flat options, prefer `ProdEuApiVm`, not `EuProdApiVm`, because it keeps one broad-to-specific order: `Environment + Region + Role + Kind`. That said, in this repo’s nested deployment style the cleaner answer is: neither. Put the environment at the parent level as `Prod`, then use region/tier zones such as `EuAppTier`, `EuDataTier`, `UsAppTier`, `UsDataTier`, and VM ids such as `euApiVm`, `euWorkerVm`, `euMongoVm`, `usApiVm`, `usWorkerVm`, `usMongoVm`. To keep everything readable, apply one convention everywhere: same token order, PascalCase for deployment node kinds, lower-camel ids for instances, `Vm` not `VM`, and stable region tokens such as `Eu` and `Us`.
